title: Autoscaler hysteresis & backoff — field notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick field notes and summary metrics from a set of targeted autoscaler experiments focusing on hysteresis windows and backoff multipliers. These cover differences across regions (us-west1 vs eu-west1), the effect of min-node sizing for KV-cache warmness, and policy interactions with burst capacity. Objective is to recommend a safe, low-cost default policy we can ship to Dedicated clusters and to capture gotchas for Private deployments.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Hysteresis (separate up/down thresholds with a small time-window) reduces oscillation without materially increasing p95 latency when min_nodes >= 2 per region.
- Aggressive backoff (scale-down multiplier > 1.5) saves cost but increases cold-start rate and p95 tail for chat workloads with long KV cache dependency.
- eu-west1 spot preemption + provisioning latency made scale-up slower by ~18s vs us-west1; we recommend raising max_burst in eu-west1 rather than aggressive scale-up triggers.

Experiment matrix (what we varied):
- Min nodes: 0, 1, 2, 4
- Max nodes: 8, 16 (kept same across experiments for comparability)
- Scale-up trigger: queue_length >= 3, GPU_util >= 55%, inferred_request_rate >= 40r/s
- Scale-down trigger: queue_length <= 1, GPU_util <= 20%
- Hysteresis window (time that trigger must persist): 30s, 60s, 120s
- Scale-down backoff multiplier (cooldown multiplier applied after a scale-down): 1.0, 1.5, 2.0
- Burst capacity: off, 10% extra nodes reserved, region-burst override
- Workloads: short-completion gen (avg 80 tokens), long-context chat (avg 1.5k tokens with KV cache warmups), embedding-only baseline

Test infra & measurement notes:
- Clusters provisioned on GCP managed instance pools (A100s for dedicated test clusters). We intentionally used a mix of on-demand and spot pools to surface preemption behavior.
- Measurements taken via the /metrics ingestion pipeline and request-trace spans; p95 measured at request level (end-to-end), cold-start flagged by instance-init span in tracing.
- Each cell in the table below is median across 3 x 30 minute runs, with synthetic traffic replayed from production traces (anonymized).

Key results table (compact):
scenario,min_nodes,max_nodes,scale_up_trigger,scale_down_trigger,hysteresis_s,backoff_mult,observed_p95_ms,cold_start_rate_pct,cost_delta_pct
base-min-1-30s,1,16,GPU>=55,GPU<=20,30,1.0,420,1.8,0.0
min-0-high-backoff,0,16,GPU>=55,GPU<=20,30,2.0,610,9.6,-12.6
min-2-long-hyst,2,16,GPU>=55,GPU<=20,120,1.0,450,0.9,-1.9
burst-eu-west,1,16,GPU>=55,GPU<=20,30,1.0,480,3.2,-0.5
queue-trigger-low,1,16,queue>=3,queue<=1,60,1.0,390,1.2,-2.8
predictive-probe,1,16,predictive>=40r/s,GPU<=20,30,1.0,370,0.6,-4.1

Notes on the table / interpretation:
- base-min-1-30s is our current-ish default for test clusters. p95 420ms, cold_start 1.8%.
- Removing a warm min node (min=0) and applying aggressive backoff (mult=2.0) reduces cost by ~12.6% but p95 jumps to 610ms and cold_start spikes to ~9.6% on long-chat traffic; many of these cold starts are KV-cache warmups that add 200–800ms depending on model and cache miss.
- Increasing min_nodes to 2 yields the best tradeoff across long-chat workloads (p95 +30ms vs base but cold_start halved and cost impact small). This supports the thesis that a small per-region warm pad is worth it for chat-heavy customers.
- Predictive trigger (request-rate probe) consistently reduced tail and cost vs pure GPU_util triggers for bursty traffic patterns. We used a smoothed EWMA probe to avoid reacting to microbursts.
- eu-west1 needed a different knob: provisioning latency + spot churn meant pure aggressive scale-up often landed late. We reduced tail by enabling region-burst=10% (pre-warmed spare capacity) rather than decreasing scale-up hysteresis.

Anomalies & gotchas observed:
- Scale-down during sustained but lightly correlated traffic across many small routes caused fragmentation: instances drained slowly, leading to token-queueing and p95 rise for ~60–90s. Hysteresis helped but drain-time tuning is also needed.
- Backoff multiplier interacts with tracing-based cold-start detection: higher multipliers increased the absolute number of cold starts but made them cluster in time, which spiked p99 more than p95. Customer dashboards will show this as short bad incidents vs continuous degradation.
- Prediction-based triggers are sensitive to model mix changes; we saw one case where a sudden shift to long-token completions (due to a test experiment) made the request-rate probe under-estimate needed capacity. We added a cheap per-route average_output_tokens estimator to the predictive model to mitigate.

Practical recommendations (what to change):
1) Default policy for Hosted/Dedicated: min_nodes=1, min_warm_cache_tag=true (prefer node assignment that keeps KV cache warm), hysteresis_up=30s, hysteresis_down=60–120s, backoff_mult=1.25. Rationale: good cost vs tail tradeoff across workloads.
2) For chat-heavy customers: recommend min_nodes>=2 and enable region-burst=5–10% to ensure fast model/kv warmups in high-latency regions.
3) For regions with high spot churn (eu-west1 in these tests): favor small reserved burst vs lowering hysteresis; add region-level preemption metric to autoscaler scoring.
4) Add a predictive trigger option in the console (request-rate smoothed probe + per-route token-length estimate) and default it to off; enable via policy toggle for customers who opt in.

Next actions & follow-ups:
- Run a 24-hour soak with chosen default (min=1, backoff=1.25, hysteresis_up=30s, hysteresis_down=90s) on two customer-facing Dedicated pools to measure real-world cost delta and p99 incidents. (Owner: Marco; target: 2025-11-10)
- Wire the "min_warm_cache_tag" into the scheduler so warm replicas get affinity to nodes with hot KV cache. (Owner: Lena; RFC in progress.)
- Add a dashboard panel showing post-scale-down cold-start spike rate (count of instance-init spans in 5m window) and add alert threshold. (Owner: Samir)

Appendix A — raw sample CSV from one run (us-west1, long-chat workload):
timestamp,total_nodes,gpu_util_avg,queue_len,requests_per_min,p95_ms,cold_start_count
2025-10-12T10:00:00Z,4,62,2,420,410,2
2025-10-12T10:03:00Z,6,78,5,720,620,6
2025-10-12T10:06:00Z,2,18,0,90,380,0

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Should we expose "min_warm_cache" as a default for small tenants? It helps tail a lot but increases baseline cost. Need finance input on threshold where this becomes revenue negative.
- Can we get faster spot re-provisioning in eu-west1 via partner images/pinned-hosttypes? Ops to investigate.

End of notes.
(These are rough/working-sheet notes — will tidy into a formal playbook if we decide to adopt the default.)
